decision_question: Which lines would not survive a five-minute probe in an interview or a reference check, and does anything read as inflated even if it is true?
verdict_rationale: The 300% sales line (R14) has no baseline, no timeframe and no link to your own work in a summer internship. Everything else is modest and checkable.
one_line_take: The 300% sales line will not survive one follow-up question; the rest holds up.

dimension_scores.note: 300% in a summer internship needs context.
Unclear who drove the sales change.

findings.title: A 300% sales claim with no baseline or method
findings.detail: 300% compared to what, over what period, and what was your part? An interviewer will ask, and a vague answer hurts every other line.

evidence.quote: Increased online sales by 300% during the summer sale

fix.suggestion: Say what you actually did for the sale, and keep the number only with its real baseline.
fix.candidate_question: What was the 300% measured against, and what did you do for the summer sale?

strengths.title: Modest, specific claims you can back up

questions_for_candidate.question: What was the 300% measured against, and what did you do for the summer sale?
questions_for_candidate.why: The claim needs a baseline and your role.

claim_audit.probe_question: What was the 300% measured against, and what was your part in it?
How did you get 140 people to answer the survey?
